summary.summary: This is the covering report introducing the Chief Finance Officer's Treasury Management 2025/26 Annual Report, which itself will go to full Council on 16 July 2026 as Annex 1; that annex (with the outturn figures, borrowing, investment maturity and prudential-indicator tables) was not included in the packet supplied to this reading, so no borrowing, CFR or investment figures could be grounded from what was read. What the covering report does confirm is two proposed amendments to the 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy: excluding Hart and Rushmoor councils from individual counterparty limits for local-authority loans, and raising the Prudential Limit for 'Long-Term Principal Investments to Mature' in 2027/28 and 2028/29. Both changes loosen existing limits rather than tighten them, which is worth a lender's attention even though the covering report gives no revised limit figures.

signals.headline: Council proposes raising the Prudential Limit for 'Long-Term Principal Investments to Mature' in 2027/28 and 2028/29, and excluding Hart and Rushmoor from individual counterparty limits, rather than tightening either
signals.why: Raising a prudential limit and loosening a counterparty concentration limit both increase the amount of exposure the council permits itself, rather than reducing risk.

news_drafts.headline: Basingstoke and Deane's auditor expects a qualified opinion, with its scope still to be decided
news_drafts.lead:
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council's external auditor, which carries out the independent check on its accounts, expects to give a qualified audit opinion, meaning it could not fully sign off the accounts. It has not yet decided which areas the qualification will cover. The position is set out in an appendix to the Audit and Accounts Committee papers for its meeting on 28 September.

The auditor is still rebuilding its assurance over the council's reserves, the money it has put aside, after earlier years in which it gave no opinion at all. Four balances are marked "to be confirmed" rather than as fully or partly assured: the General Fund Balance, the Revaluation Reserve, the Capital Adjustment Account and the Pooled Investments Fund.

The paper says: "Although a qualification is anticipated, the basis and scope of that qualification will be determined upon completion of the remaining audit procedures." The rebuilding work was commissioned under the audit recovery programme of the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government.

findings.headline: Q1 forecast shows £0.02M overspend against budgeted surplus, signalling emerging pressures to be addressed in Medium Term Financial Strategy update.
findings.detail: Council budgeted a £0.13M surplus but Q1 monitoring indicates £0.02M adverse variance, reducing forecast surplus to £0.11M. Council acknowledges pressures facing the sector and states need to manage financial pressures through remainder of year and MTFS period. Pressures emerge across housing benefits, waste, and inflation-driven costs.
findings.matters: Demonstrates emerging pressures from housing subsidy, service inflation, and cost base growth, though council remains in surplus.
findings.figures: £0.02M adverse variance; budgeted surplus £0.13M, forecast surplus £0.11M
findings.quote: The position at this stage in the financial year reflects the pressures facing the sector and the wider economy. There is work to do manage the financial pressures over the remainder of the financial year and the period of the Council's medium term financial strategy.

findings.headline: Property portfolio showing mixed results: Industrial/Commercial £0.30M favourable offset by Malls £0.19M adverse variance.
findings.detail: Industrial and Commercial property forecast benefits from anticipated favourable rent reviews and improved lettings despite void units at lease expiry. The Malls show weaker performance with vacant units and increased business rates driving lower income than budget. Council holds reserve to mitigate adverse rent events.
findings.matters: Property income volatility flagged as ongoing risk requiring close scrutiny; demonstrates both upside and downside exposure.
findings.figures: Industrial/Commercial £0.30M favourable; Malls £0.19M adverse; council holds reserve for adverse rent events
findings.quote: Rent shortfalls have arisen this financial year due to properties becoming void at lease expiry, however these are expected to be exceeded by anticipated favourable rent reviews and improved letting expectations in other properties. The council holds a reserve against the risk of specific adverse rent events.

findings.headline: Income payment processing costs increased by £0.08M from card transaction fees and digital transaction growth.
findings.detail: Card transaction processing prices have risen, and transaction volumes increased from digital shift and growth in council tax accounts administered. Banking charges remain relatively stable.
findings.matters: Reflects ongoing cost of digital transformation and service growth; likely to persist as structural pressure.
findings.quote: The cost to the council of income payment processing has increased substantially, resulting in this overspend. This is due in part to rising prices for card transaction processing on income collected, and also to increases in transactions volumes which reflect the continued shift to digital and growth in the number of council tax accounts administered.

findings.headline: Electoral registration postage costs forecast to overspend by £0.12M as inflation in postage exceeds mitigation efforts.
findings.detail: Overspend driven by increased postage costs for electoral registration. Council is exploring alternative solutions but cannot fully mitigate cost increases that exceed inflation. This is a statutory service the council cannot avoid.
findings.matters: Demonstrates inflation pressures in mandatory non-discretionary services that pose ongoing budget risk.
findings.figures: £0.12M adverse variance; cost increases exceed inflation
findings.quote: This overspend is primarily due to postage costs for electoral registration. Alternative solutions are being accessed where possible to do so, but this cannot fully mitigate the costs increases which exceed inflation.

findings.headline: Waste collection forecast to overspend by £0.37M due to fleet retention ahead of autumn 2026 service changes.
findings.detail: Council retains existing fleet to maximise vehicle life pending waste collection changes in autumn 2026, creating £0.32M accounting charge overspend. Lower than budgeted bulky waste collections (£0.05M shortfall) indicate less waste arising in the borough.
findings.matters: Substantial cost but acknowledged as temporary; demonstrates planned service transition and shows reduced waste demand.
findings.figures: £0.37M total variance: £0.32M fleet accounting charge, £0.05M bulky waste shortfall
findings.quote: The council continues to retain existing fleet ahead of the changes to waste collections in autumn 2026. This ensures the life of those vehicles is maximised but results in an overspend of £0.32M in respect of the accounting charge for their use.
